Subject: Competitive bake-off recap: Redwood vs. Competitors (OmniHealth)

Hi Sara & Tim,

Thanks again for taking time today — good conversation. Quick recap from our side and agreed next steps so we have a single source of truth going into the testing phase.

1) Key pain points you shared
- High per-call latency on current vendor during peak hours (avg 700-900ms on 8k context) impacting clinician workflows.
- Cost variability and difficulty forecasting monthly spend as usage scales.
- Need for on-prem / VPC deployment options for PHI-sensitive workloads and auditability for SOC2 / HITRUST evidence.

2) Goals you outlined
- Sub-200ms 95th percentile latency for short inference requests (~256 tokens) in primary region.
- Predictable cost per 1k tokens with reserved capacity option considered.
- E2E audit logs + key management for at-rest/in-transit encryption.

3) Decision criteria (weighted) you gave us
- Latency (35%)
- Cost predictability (25%)
- Security/compliance posture (20%)
- Integration/Dev DX (10%)
- Support & SLA (10%)

4) What Redwood will deliver for bake-off
- A short test plan with 3 canonical prompts and traffic profile (attached scorecard).
- Two deployment options: Hosted (fastest path) and Private VPC preview for SOC2-sensitive flow.
- A customized performance run during your peak window next Thursday (9/30) with live latency metrics and token-level cost breakdown.
- Proposal v2 (attached) reflecting a reserved-capacity option if results meet thresholds.

Open questions we noted
- Which data subsets must stay on-prem for initial test? (identifiers or full records?)
- Do you have an existing KMS/HSM vendor we need to integrate with for the VPC proof of concept?

Next steps (as discussed)
- Sara: confirm team for the test (engineer + compliance) and whether sample data can be used or needs to be masked — by EOD Wed (9/23).
- Tim: confirm peak window and traffic profile for the test (we proposed 9/30 9\u201311am PT) — by Tue (9/22).
- Marissa/Aditya: share test plan + scorecard and schedule runbook review — today.

Attachments: omnibakeoff-scorecard.xlsx (test prompts, metrics to capture), redwood-proposal-v2.pdf (pricing + reserved capacity options).

If you'd like, we can also set a short 20-min alignment before the run to walk through the scorecard.

Thanks — looking forward to the test.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Marissa — appreciate the write-up. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Data scope: For the initial run we'd prefer to use masked records (PHI removed) — our compliance lead prefers not to send full EHR extracts for the first test. We'll provide a masked dataset by 9/24.

2) KMS/HSM: We use AWS KMS (Customer managed keys) today — if Redwood's VPC option requires a key integration we need the list of required permissions.

3) Latency targets: The sub-200ms 95p is our target for short calls; we understand longer context calls will be higher. Please confirm your measurement methodology (cold vs warm cache, percentile calc).

4) Competitors: We ran initial tests with VendorX and VendorY; VendorX had better P95 but worse cost predictability. Would like Redwood to focus on consistent P95 across sustained load (not just single-shot).

We can confirm the 9/30 9\u201311am PT window once we have the traffic profile.

Thanks,
Tim

Thanks Tim — great questions. Short answers inline and next steps below.

1) Data scope: Masked dataset works perfectly for the initial performance run — thanks for doing that.

2) KMS/HSM: We support AWS KMS (CMK) in the VPC/private deployment. I'll attach an integration checklist with the required IAM permissions and network config.

3) Measurement methodology (how we'll calculate P95)
- We'll run the test with a steady traffic profile that matches your peak mix (we'll use your sample traces).
- Warm cache run: we do a 20-minute warmup to populate the KV cache, then run the 1-hour sustained test for metrics.
- P95 will be computed on the request latency distribution (end-to-end from API gateway ingress to token finish). We'll provide token-level breakdowns and bucketed percentiles.

4) Focus for bake-off: We'll prioritize consistency under sustained load and provide runner-up metrics for competitors as you requested.

Attached: omnibakeoff-scorecard.xlsx (updated with runbook), redwood-provisioning-kms-checklist.pdf (integration checklist).

Next steps:
- Sara: confirm masked dataset delivery by 9/24.
- Tim: send traffic profile/trace by 9/22 (or confirm 9/30 window).
- Marissa/Aditya: schedule 20-min runbook walk-through — propose Wed 9/29 at 10am PT.

I'll follow up with invites once you confirm.

Best,
Marissa
